_comment: Recurring engine-artifact corrections, surfaced automatically in `--facts` output (per circle, as `caveats`). These encode the 'engine blind spot — override in your reading' findings accumulated in docs/lexicon/ so the AI applies them consistently instead of re-deriving them each analysis. Each rule's `when` is matched against a circle's facts; if it matches, `note` (+ `source`) is attached. This is a CORRECTION layer, not an effect claim. Add a rule here when a lexicon Finding records an artifact that recurs across spells. Predicates supported by tools/spell-engine-cli.mjs evalCaveat(): coreElement[], sign, minCount, inverted, operatorKind, symmetry[], signCountEquals, hasUnknownSigns.

caveats.note: 4+ balanced Columns: the engine's `aim`/'above the seal' label is a KNOWN ARTIFACT. Balanced Columns confine/shape the flow (and spread omnidirectionally if inverted) — they do NOT beam in a compass direction. Read the aim as out-of-plane (up) or as containment, per substance.

Levitation on water/fire/light lifts VERTICALLY without steering. The engine routes every directional sign through aim/spin math, so any reported lateral `aim` or `spin` here is spurious — treat as artifact.

An inverted Column's spread closely matches Dispersion's; canon cannot distinguish the two. Read it as omnidirectional eruption and FLAG the uncertainty rather than inventing a difference from Dispersion.

Dispersion's outward leak is canonically indistinguishable from an inverted Column. Note the spread is the same and flag the uncertainty; whether it is directional or semi-directional is also unresolved in canon.
A single sign read slightly off-origin can false-flag `asymmetric`/unstable. With one sign, treat the symmetry/stability flag as unreliable.
This circle contains an unidentified (`unknown_*`) sign. Any deduction is necessarily INCOMPLETE — say so, reason its likely role from its drawing geometry, and do not assert a confident effect.
